title: Bangladesh PM says Hasina's party serves 'masters' across the border as unrest spreads
dek: Tarique Rahman did not name India, where Sheikh Hasina has lived since 2024, but accused the banned Awami League of conspiring to please its hosts. Dhaka police made 474 more arrests; New Delhi has not responded.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Bangladesh's Prime Minister, Tarique Rahman, has accused the banned Awami League of acting on behalf of "the country across the border", in remarks widely read as aimed at India, as a week of arson and bomb attacks by supporters of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina spread to more than 20 districts and police in Dhaka reported 474 more arrests in a single day.

"The country across the border, where they have fled to, is their master," Rahman told a public meeting in Lalmonirhat, in northern Bangladesh on the border with West Bengal's Cooch Behar district, on Thursday, according to reports. He did not name India, where Ms Hasina has lived since she was forced from power in August 2024, but said Awami League leaders had "not looked at the interests of Bangladesh and its people" and were "conspiring to keep their masters happy", according to reports. India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) did not immediately respond to requests for comment, according to reports, and had issued no statement by Friday afternoon.

## What happened

Rahman spoke on the day of a dawn-to-dusk "lockdown" called by the Awami League, whose political activities have been banned since May 2025. The shutdown was most effective in the southern and south-western districts where the party is strongest, according to reports, and was marked by arson attacks on police stations, MPs' homes, buses and offices, and blockades of highways and railway lines.

"Bangladeshis did not fight the Liberation War in 1971 or lead the uprising in 2024 to submit to anyone," Rahman said, according to reports. In parliament a day earlier he had called the Awami League "not a political party, but a terrorist group", described Ms Hasina as the "fugitive leader of the terrorist party" and accused her of ordering arson attacks on the homes of political opponents, according to reports. "Please do not give in to any provocation," he told the public. He also urged lawmakers of his Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) to mobilise party workers on the streets rather than rely only on the administration, according to reports.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police said on Friday that it had arrested 474 people in the capital in the previous 24 hours and filed 48 cases, in raids "targeting members of the banned groups and those involved in sabotage", according to reports. Of those arrested, 124 were reported to belong to the Awami League and its affiliates. That followed 537 arrests, 107 of them Awami League members, in the 24 hours to Thursday morning, according to reports; the figures cover separate periods.

The government has also asked for Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) troops to be deployed nationwide from Friday. A home ministry letter to the police chief warned of "a risk of political tension, counter-programmes and deterioration of law and order", according to reports. On Thursday about 3,000 BGB personnel were deployed in seven districts.

## The toll

At least four people were killed between 17 and 18 November, according to a tally of the week's violence by one Dhaka newspaper: a leader of the BNP's farmers' wing who suffered burns during an attack on a highway blockade in Faridpur's Bhanga, two leaders of BNP-affiliated groups killed when a motorcycle procession was attacked in Narail's Kalia, and a bus worker who died of burns after two buses were set on fire in Pirojpur's Bhandaria. Reports differ: one put the toll from the unrest at at least five.

Bombings, arson, road blockades or clashes were reported in at least 21 districts between 14 and 19 November, according to reports. Police headquarters recorded 70 crude bomb explosions and 57 arson attacks on vehicles nationwide between 7 and 17 November, according to reports. In Gopalganj, Ms Hasina's home district, the Tungipara police station was set on fire on 17 November and the Muksudpur police station on 19 November; both remained shut on Friday, although the district had calmed, according to reports. Part of the ancestral home of Muhammad Yunus, the Nobel laureate who led the interim government after Ms Hasina's fall, was set on fire in Chattogram late on Wednesday; police said flammable material was probably thrown into an unused ground-floor room, and relatives living upstairs were unhurt, according to reports. Early on Friday, attackers tried to set fire to the gate of a state minister's home in Sylhet, according to reports.

The Awami League has announced "continuous programmes" from Friday and a 48-hour lockdown on 29 and 30 November, according to one report; this has not been confirmed by the party in Bangladesh.

## Background

Ms Hasina, 79, led Bangladesh for 15 years until a student-led uprising in August 2024, and fled to India. A special tribunal in Dhaka sentenced her to death in absentia for crimes against humanity a year ago; Thursday's lockdown coincided with the anniversary of that verdict. Dhaka has asked New Delhi to extradite her, and India has said the request is being examined under its legal procedures. The BNP won the general election in February 2026, bringing Rahman to power.

The latest protests began after the government rejected Ms Hasina's application for a new passport, which she needs in order to travel, according to reports. She has said she will return to Bangladesh in December "at any cost". Bangladesh's Law Minister, Md Asaduzzaman, has said she will come back "through legal means", meaning to face the courts.

## Why it matters for India and Bengal

Rahman's remarks are the sharpest suggestion yet from his government that India is sheltering those it blames for the violence, and they come at a delicate time. The joint committee under the Ganges Water Treaty meets in Dhaka from 21 to 23 November, with the 30-year treaty due to expire on 12 December and no agreement yet on renewing it. Water sharing at Farakka directly affects West Bengal and the Kolkata port.

The worst-hit districts, including Gopalganj, Faridpur, Narail and Pirojpur, lie in south-western Bangladesh, close to West Bengal's North and South 24 Parganas and Nadia. Lalmonirhat, where Rahman spoke, borders Cooch Behar. Any sustained crackdown, or a flight of people, would be felt first along Bengal's border. On Friday, the BGB said it had stopped what it called a "push-in" of four men by the Border Security Force at Meherpur, opposite Nadia; the BSF has not commented.

## What happens next

- 21-23 November: Ganges Water Treaty joint committee meeting in Dhaka
- 29-30 November: 48-hour lockdown reported to have been called by the Awami League
- December: Ms Hasina's declared return
- 12 December: Ganges Water Treaty expires unless renewed
